title: Obstetric anaesthesia in spontaneous delivery and caesarean section, and the influence of general and anaesthesiological factors on maternal and neonatal outcomes (PDA-NEO - Subgroup analysis of the PDA-AUX study)
summary:
During a caesarean section or a vaginal birth, the anaesthesia or pain relief given to the mother may also affect the newborn. Recent studies point to this and recommend considering mother and child in obstetric analysis. This requires linking the mothers’ data with the newborns’ data.

The Ethics Committee has therefore approved linking the data of the PDA-AUX study with the corresponding newborn data for the years 2017–2024. The analysis is carried out as a sub-study called PDA-NEO.

Using anonymised, routinely collected clinical data, the study examines whether the anaesthetic technique used for caesarean section and the urgency of the procedure are associated with the newborn’s condition after birth. For vaginal births, it examines whether an epidural placed during labour is associated with severe perineal tears and with the newborn’s condition, and whether delivery by vacuum or forceps modifies this association. No additional examinations or interventions are performed in patients or children. The results are intended to provide indications for further, in particular prospective, studies.
